chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Decca and Vocalion records with Gene Sedric, Mabel Robinson and Sam Price
summary: Between Fats's engagements he recorded for Decca and Vocalion with Sedric, a singer and Sam Price; he says those dates were not simply Fats's band without Fats.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I tell you, while you're thinking of that, something else I want to ask you. That is -- I guess it must have been in the forties, you were making some records for Decca, and for Vocalion, with Mabel Robinson, Sam Price, with Gene Sedric. When were those records? Were those when you were with Fats?

I don't think so. I don't think so. It's in between, you know, because they had -- when you had those lay-offs, and you got a club date, or record date, I mean where -- whenever, wherever, you appreciated it, and you went the heck on it, and did it. And you got paid, and they don't worry about you anymore, and you don't worry about them. Hey, I'm paid, you happy, good-bye. You know.
Well, the records you made with Gene Sedric, for example, that was basically Fats' band without Fats, wasn't it?
No, no. No, 'no, no. Whatever comes in, the name that's being offered, that they're selling,

that's it. You know. In other words, you -- I couldn't record the group and say well, even Fats Waller, this is Herman Autrey with Fats' group, and expect anything to roll off on me, from Fats, to help me on, because it -- well, it's up to you to do something, what are you doing? What you got? What you got to offer? Something, or nothing? You know. One of those things.
I got that out of a book. It says you were on a record with her, 'Me and My Chauffeur', and 'I've Got Too Many Blues', on Decca. And with Sam Price -- I know Sam, but of course he made --
Yeah, I did those things for Decca.
-- 'Blow, Katie, Blow', and 'It's All Right, Jack.'
Yeah, I think I remember now. Let's see, I know Sam, and maybe -- whoof-foof-foof-foof.
